title: Reading Sensor Data
summary: Let's stream live sensor telemetry straight into your computer's screen using the Arduino IDE Serial Monitor!

steps.title: Reading Sensor Data

quickCheck.question: Which command in `setup()` opens the serial data channel so your computer can display sensor telemetry?
quickCheck.explanation: Serial.begin(9600) sets the communication speed (baud rate) and opens the serial channel between the Arduino and computer.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: From Lesson 4 & 6: Serial.begin(9600) is the handshake that lets your Arduino talk to the Serial Monitor at 9600 bits per second.

quickCheck.question: What happens if the baud rate selected in the Arduino IDE Serial Monitor does not match `Serial.begin()` in your code?
options: The telemetry will appear as garbled symbols, gibberish, or blank lines
The Arduino microcontroller chip will be permanently damaged
The sensor will stop measuring physical values
quickCheck.explanation: When baud rates mismatch, the computer and Arduino sample bits at different speeds, resulting in garbled characters or blank text.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Both sides must agree on the exact same speed (like 9600 baud) to understand each other's data signals.
